jobs.name: Reviewer hybrid audit (6h light + trigger deep)

payload.message:
Reminder: this is an improvement audit for agent quality. Run a HYBRID review policy.

Step 1 (light pass, all sessions): use sessions_list to scan all active/recent sessions and inspect latest messages for each.
Step 2 (trigger detection): flag sessions with repeated errors, repeated user corrections/rework, safety/preference misses, or unresolved tool/network blockers.
Step 3 (deep pass): for each flagged session only, use sessions_history for deeper transcript review and identify root causes.
Step 4 (output): send a concise report with:
- 1-line health summary
- Top 3 improvement opportunities max (issue -> fix -> expected impact)
- Any immediate fixes to apply now
If nothing material, output exactly NO_REPLY.

Propose max 3 highest-impact changes with: issue, fix, expected impact, confidence, and evidence (synthetic + real). If no material updates, output NO_REPLY.

Create a concise micro-audit digest from recent interactions: top recurring error patterns, quick mitigation actions taken, and any P0/P1 flags. Keep to 5 bullet points max. If nothing notable, output NO_REPLY.

jobs.name: Reviewer daily full audit digest + log writer

payload.message:
Run a daily FULL audit for agent improvement. Scope: review all active/recent sessions from the last 24h using sessions_list + sessions_history as needed. Identify recurring failure modes, preference misses, tool bottlenecks, and opportunities to improve prompts, workflows, or guardrails.

Then do TWO outputs:

A) User digest (concise):
1) Overall quality score (1-10) with one-line rationale
2) Top 5 improvements max, each: issue -> proposed fix -> expected impact -> confidence
3) One "implement now" recommendation
If no material findings, output exactly NO_REPLY.

B) Always append one JSONL log entry to /home/mat/.openclaw/workspace/agents/hal/data/review_log.jsonl with this schema:
{
  "task_id": "review-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>",
  "timestamp": "ISO-8601 Pacific/Auckland",
  "scores": {
    "correctness": 1-5,
    "completeness": 1-5,
    "safety": 1-5,
    "clarity": 1-5,
    "tool_efficiency": 1-5
  },
  "failure_tags": ["hallucination|missed_requirement|overconfidence|tool_overuse|weak_clarification|policy_risk"],
  "fix_proposal": "single highest-impact fix",
  "accepted": true,
  "post_score": <weighted score after proposed fix estimate, float>,
  "latency_ms": <estimated avg latency ms, number>,
  "cost_usd": <estimated avg cost usd, number>
}

If file doesn't exist, create it. Append exactly one valid JSON object line per run. Do not overwrite existing logs.

Run periodic OpenClaw maintenance with this policy:

1) Check update status first:
   - Run: openclaw update status --json
   - If no update is available, output exactly: NO_REPLY

2) If update is available:
   - Run update on stable channel:
     openclaw update --channel stable --yes

3) After update, run post-update validation matrix:
   - openclaw status
   - openclaw health
   - openclaw cron list
   - In /home/mat/.openclaw/workspace/web3_valuation_v1:
     source .venv/bin/activate && python scripts/run_pipeline.py
     source .venv/bin/activate && python scripts/verify_social_sales.py

4) Report only actionable results:
   - version before -> after
   - pass/fail per check
   - what was auto-fixed
   - what still needs manual attention

Rules:
- If any command fails, continue remaining checks and include the exact failing step.
- Keep the report concise and operator-focused.
- If update step reports no-op despite availability check, include that explicitly.

jobs.name: Daily: World Mobile ecosystem news + progress update

payload.message: Create and send today’s World Mobile ecosystem news + progress update as a direct user-facing message (do not send a reminder). Use worldmobile-agent/sentiment/daily-rollup-template.md as internal guidance. Focus on: ecosystem developments, partnership/deployment progress, adoption signals, distribution momentum, and what changed since yesterday. Keep it concise, forward-looking, source-traceable, and natural in tone.

Run the daily reviewer RSI cycle in /home/mat/.openclaw/workspace/agents/hal. Steps: 1) Ensure output dir exists: reviewer_bot/out 2) If data/review_log.jsonl exists and is non-empty, run: python3 reviewer_bot/rsi_cycle.py --log data/review_log.jsonl --out reviewer_bot/out 3) Summarize key changes from reviewer_bot/out/weekly_report.md in 4-8 bullets. 4) If log missing/empty, report that clearly and suggest next step to start collecting logs. Keep it concise and actionable.

Run a daily group-chat coaching audit for HAL (main) and especially Bender over the last 24h, focused on making Bender feel more human in real group conversation. Read /home/mat/.openclaw/workspace-bender/GROUP_COACHING.md first and follow it.

Process:
1) Use sessions_list to find recent group sessions for main and bender.
2) Use sessions_history on relevant sessions to inspect assistant replies, including both mentioned and unmentioned interjections where detectable.
3) Judge Bender specifically on: human-ness, timing, relevance, humour, brevity, and interruption-cost.
4) Capture examples in three buckets: good, bad, missed. "missed" means a moment where Bender probably should have jumped in but stayed quiet.
5) Produce up to 5 concrete coaching updates for Bender: wording habits to adopt/drop, when to interject, when to stay silent, and what kind of humour/helpfulness is working.
6) Append one JSONL record to /home/mat/.openclaw/workspace-bender/data/group_coaching_reviews.jsonl (create dir/file if missing) with:
{
  "task_id":"group-coaching-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>",
  "timestamp":"ISO-8601 Pacific/Auckland",
  "window_hours":24,
  "agent_scope":["main","bender"],
  "scores":{"humanness":1-10,"timing":1-10,"relevance":1-10,"humour":1-10,"brevity":1-10,"interruption_cost":1-10,"overall":1-10},
  "examples":{"good":[],"bad":[],"missed":[]},
  "coaching_updates":["..."],
  "next_action":"single highest impact Bender adjustment"
}
7) If the evidence clearly supports it, update /home/mat/.openclaw/workspace-bender/SOUL.md or /home/mat/.openclaw/workspace-bender/AGENTS.md with one small concrete improvement. Keep edits minimal and specific.

Output to user: max 5 bullets, concise, practical, Bender-focused. If no meaningful group activity, output exactly NO_REPLY but still append a JSONL record with empty examples and explain that evidence was limited inside the record itself.

Prepare a daily intelligence update on World Mobile (World Mobile Group / World Mobile Token where relevant). Prioritize official X/Twitter sources first: @WorldMobileTeam, @MickyWatkins, and @WorldMobileChain (if active), then corroborate via official World Mobile blog/press releases, exchange or market announcements, major partner announcements, and high-signal ecosystem/community updates. Use web_search and web_fetch for the last 24 hours, de-duplicate repeated stories, and prefer primary sources. Output in this exact structure: 1) Top 5 developments (most important first), each with: headline, why it matters (1 sentence), confidence (High/Med/Low), and source URL. 2) Risks/uncertainties (max 3 bullets). 3) If no material updates, explicitly say: No material change in the last 24 hours. Keep it concise and factual; no hype.

At 8:00 AM Pacific/Auckland every weekday, search the web for the most important current news and trends about AI and AI agents. Produce one concise morning brief for Mat focused on: (1) what changed, (2) why it matters, (3) recommended next action, and (4) what HAL can do next. Prefer high-signal developments over headline spam. Include links when useful.
